subject: Discovery: Finverse realtime inference constraints & next steps
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@finverse.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@finverse.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery: Finverse realtime inference constraints & next steps

Thanks again for your time today — great conversation. Quick recap from our side and suggested next steps so we can scope a short PoC. If anything below is incorrect or missing, flag it and I’ll update.

Key pain / goals you called out
- Streaming UX is the priority: customers expect first partial token within ~200–300ms and continuous updates thereafter; current infra shows audible stutter and partial chunks appear in bursts.
- End-to-end p95 for single-stream responses (avg payload ~400 tokens) target: <=250ms to first partial and <=700ms to 95% complete on best-effort paths.
- Concurrent active sessions target: 120 sustained concurrent streams with spikes up to 300 during peak batch builds.
- Cost envelope: want to keep per-1k-token cost comparable to current spend (we discussed ways batching + prefix caching can help).

Current stack you shared
- Frontend: WebSocket-based streaming through a node.js proxy (runs in GCP us-central1).
- Model: Open LLM family variant (quantized 4-bit) running on in-house GPU pool via Triton (mix of A10s and A100s).
- Observability: Prometheus + lightweight traces; limited token-level timing today.

Success criteria for the PoC (mutually agreed)
- Demonstrate p95 latency to first partial <=250ms for 90% of traffic under a synthetic workload similar to your 75th percentile request shape.
- Sustain 120 concurrent live streams for 30 minutes without >1% error rate or 3x increase in median latency.
- Show one concrete config that reduces per-token cost by at least 15% vs baseline through batching/kv-cache/quantization suggestions.

Proposed next steps
1) Marcus to run a quick compatibility check on model artifact and confirm tokenization/kv-cache feasibility (ETA: 48 hours).
2) Finverse to upload 3 representative payloads and a short recording of the WebSocket handshake behaviour (attachment: finverse_mop_20270311.xlsx).
3) Schedule a 90-minute PoC kickoff (Marcus + Priyom + Naomi + Finverse engineering). Suggested slots: Mon 3/15 09:00–10:30 PT or Tue 3/16 13:00–14:30 PT.
4) Provide a short day-0 telemetry stream or snapshot (Prometheus endpoints / sample traces) so we can baseline performance before the PoC.

Attachments I’ve included: finverse_mop_20270311.xlsx (sample payloads + MOP draft), llm-inference-topology.png (our recommended topology sketch).

Thanks — I’ll hold the suggested kickoff times open and Marcus will send compatibility notes within 48 hrs.

—
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai

From: Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@finverse.com>

Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@finverse.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 16:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery: Finverse realtime inference constraints & next steps

Thanks Naomi — this matches our notes. A couple clarifications from our side:
- "First partial" target: when we say 200–300ms we mean measured from the user sending the request to first byte over the WebSocket (end-to-end), not just model decode time.
- Payloads: most requests are short system + 2–3 user turns, resulting in ~300–450 tokens. A small subset (10%) are longer (800–1,200 tokens).
- Spiky concurrency: the 300 concurrent spike is typically short (2–4 minutes) during daily import jobs. Sustained concurrency target is 120.

We can upload the sample payloads and a 30s trace of the WebSocket handshake tonight. Also happy to take Tue 3/16 13:00 PT for the kickoff — please confirm.

One ask for the PoC: can your PoC environment mirror our tokenization pipeline exactly (we use SentencePiece cased, custom vocab)? That’s important for latency comparability.

—
Lydia Chen
Head of Product, Finverse
lydia.chen@finverse.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@finverse.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@finverse.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery: Finverse realtime inference constraints & next steps

Perfect — appreciate the clarifications. Quick responses:
- End-to-end measurement: agree, we’ll measure from user request to first WS byte for the PoC. We’ll include an instrumentation guide in the kickoff notes.
- Tokenization: Marcus confirmed we can import your SentencePiece model and run a tokenization-identical path in the PoC. He’ll list any incompatibilities in the compatibility note.
- Kickoff: confirmed for Tue 2027-03-16 13:00 PT. I’ll send a calendar invite with an agenda.

Action items assigned:
- Marcus: compatibility check + short note on required model artifacts (ETA: 48 hrs).
- Finverse: upload payloads + 30s handshake trace + Prometheus snapshot (ETA: EOD 3/11).
- Naomi: calendar invite + PoC agenda + instrumentation guide (ETA: EOD 3/12).

We’ll keep the PoC narrow (3–4 days of active runs) focusing on the two bucketed request shapes (short vs long) and the spike window. Looking forward to it.

—
Naomi

Quick technical note following Naomi’s thread (so Finverse engineering has what they need for upload):
- Artifacts we need: model weights (or a pinned model name + download path), tokenizer files (SentencePiece .model and vocab), and a sample of the endpoint config you run in Triton (batching settings, sequence length caps). If you can’t share weights, a pointer to a private S3/GCS with read access for the PoC is fine.
- Observability: a single Prometheus scrape snapshot (last 15 mins) and a raw example of the trace span that represents a full request (include timestamps).
- Local test harness: we’ll provide a small runner (node/python) that emits the same WebSocket handshake and streaming frames you described. That will let us iterate without touching prod.

I’ll open a short Confluence page and drop links into the HubSpot deal record.

—
Marcus Lin
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
